Export the data of an occupancy model with false positives

Source: R/export_occupancy.R
export_occupancy_data.Rd

Writes, in one folder, everything an occupancy model with false positives needs from a passive acoustic survey: the occasions, the classifier scores, the reviewed clips with their sampling design and, optionally, covariates of the occasions and posterior draws of a Bayesian calibration. The folder follows the sheepdog-occupancy schema, version 1.1, described in vignette("crywolf-integration"); the crywolf package reads it, but any software can, since every table is a plain CSV file (the calibration draws are a Parquet file).

Usage

export_occupancy_data(
  output_dir,
  detections,
  recordings = NULL,
  validation = NULL,
  fit = NULL,
  sites = NULL,
  occasion_covariates = NULL,
  calibration_keys = NULL,
  occasion_unit = c("file", "minute"),
  recording_duration = NULL,
  min_confidence = 0.1,
  dawn_hour = 12,
  species = NULL,
  n_draws = 100,
  grid_step = 0.01,
  seed = 2026,
  audio_pattern = "\\.(wav|flac|mp3)$",
  remap_from = NULL,
  remap_to = NULL,
  classifier = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

output_dir

Folder to write. Created if needed.

detections

Predictions, as returned by read_selection_tables().

recordings

The list of all recordings, as a data frame or the path to a CSV file with the columns site and source_audio, as in select_clips(). NULL lists the audio files in the folders of the recordings that have predictions, which then must be reachable (see remap_from).

validation

Reviewed clips: paths to validation_by_clip.csv files (output of post_validation()) or a data frame with their columns, e.g. from read_validation_tables() or consensus_verdicts(). NULL writes no validation tables.

fit

Optional model from fit_calibration() with engine = "brms", for calibration_draws.parquet.

sites

Optional data frame of site covariates, with a site column.

occasion_covariates

Optional data frame of covariates of the occasions (e.g. temperature or the month), with site and either occasion_id or source_audio (plus start, in s, for minute occasions). One row per occasion; occasions without a row get NA. Columns named like those of occasions.csv are refused.

calibration_keys

Optional grouping variables of the calibration model, besides site and species, that vary between occasions (see Calibration keys). Only used with fit.

occasion_unit

The occasion of the occupancy model: "file" (a recording) or "minute". Use the value of the clip extraction, so that the occasion_id of the reviewed clips match.

recording_duration

Length of the recordings (s). Needed for minute occasions unless the 'av' package can read the files.

min_confidence

Predictions below this confidence are not written; it is also the lower end of the grid of the calibration draws. Use the min_confidence of the BirdNET run or higher.

dawn_hour

Recordings that start before this hour belong to the night before.

species

Restrict to these short species codes (the last part of species_code, e.g. "boa-ran"). NULL keeps all.

n_draws

Number of posterior draws of the calibration.

grid_step

Step of the grid of scores of the calibration draws.

seed

Seed of the choice of draws. The global random number generator is left as it was.

audio_pattern

Regular expression for the audio files listed when recordings is NULL.

remap_from, remap_to

Replace the prefix remap_from of the begin_path paths by remap_to, e.g. "N:/" and "/Volumes/Arara/". Backslashes are turned into forward slashes first.

classifier

Optional label of the classifier, recorded in schema.json.

overwrite

Replace an existing export in output_dir?

Value

Invisibly, a list with the tables written (tibbles) and the schema (a list).

Tables

  • occasions.csv: one row per occasion (a recording, or a minute of a recording), with or without predictions, followed by the columns of occasion_covariates and of the calibration keys.

  • detections.csv: one row per prediction with confidence >= min_confidence.

  • scores.csv: one row per occasion x species with at least one prediction: the highest score and the number of predictions. Occasion x species pairs absent from this table had no prediction >= min_confidence (a censored score).

  • validation.csv: the reviewed clips of the "top" and "random_detections" designs, with their verdict and inclusion probability (only when validation is given).

  • recordings_verified.csv: the occasions annotated by ear in the "random_recordings" design, with the state of each occasion (only when validation holds such clips).

  • sites.csv: one row per site, with the covariates of sites.

  • calibration_draws.parquet: posterior draws of P(TP) on a grid of scores for each site x species with predictions, and for each level of the calibration_keys found among the occasions of the site (only when fit is given; needs the 'arrow' package).

  • schema.json: name and version of the schema, the settings of the export, the lists of sites and species and the number of rows of each table.

Calibration keys. A calibration may depend on a property of the occasion besides site and species, such as the month of the recording (tp ~ logit_conf + (1 | month)). Name such grouping variables in calibration_keys: each becomes a text column of occasions.csv and of calibration_draws.parquet, so that a reader matches each prediction to the draws of its occasion. A key must be a column of occasion_covariates, except "month", which is derived from the recording date (YYYYMM) when not given. Levels absent from the calibration data are drawn as new levels of the group (brms sample_new_levels = "uncertainty"); occasions without a value of a key are reported, since their predictions cannot be scored.

Two checks guard against inputs that would inflate the detections: predictions repeating the site, recording, offset and species of another (e.g. a selection table read twice) are dropped with a warning, and a warning is given when most occasion x species with several predictions have the same score in all of them, a sign that one score per occasion was copied to several rows.

A clip verdict and the state of an occasion are kept apart on purpose: a positive clip proves that the species called in its occasion, but a negative clip only says that this prediction was a false positive (the species may still have called, with a lower score). A recording annotated by ear gives the state of the whole occasion.

See also

vignette("crywolf-integration") for the columns of each table.
